name: CASIA VasCure
full_name: CASIA vascular robotic system: Dual-finger Robotic Hand (DRH) and VasCure two-channel PCI robot
group: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA), State Key Lab of Management and Control for Complex Systems / Multimodal AI Systems (Zeng-Guang Hou, Xiao-Liang Xie, Xiao-Hu Zhou, Shi-Qi Liu, Gui-Bin Bian); animal tests at Shanghai Huadong Hospital
versions: 2011 image-based guidewire navigation and delivery system (ji2011_guidewire, title); 2013 enhanced dual-finger robotic hand for catheter (bian2013_enhanced, title); 2015 dual-finger robotic hand (DRH): bionic thumb (driven roller, 2 DOF) and bionic forefinger (passive roller, 3 DOF); rotating the rollers about their axes advances the device, translating them in opposite directions along their axes rolls it; two steppers, guidewire gripper, console with handle and LCD panel; bench tests with EM tracking (feng2015_bioinspired, full: Sec. II-A, II-B, III); motion-scaling control (feng2015_motion abstract); 2020 Dual-finger Robotic Hand for Angioplasty, DRH: bionic thumb + bionic forefinger rollers on two steppers, DC-motor clamping, guidewire gripper (wei2020_novel Sec. 2, full); 2021 VasCure: one active + two passive rollers = two channels for two guidewires, graspers A/B, slave on a robot arm (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II, full) and 5G version with generalized predictive control (zhang2021_improved, abstract); 2023-2025 same platform in a white/blue housing on an arm used for learning-based delivery (li2024_modelbased Fig. 2; li2023_casog; li2023_discrete; wang2025_fuzzy); VasCure
target_anatomy: coronary (PCI; bifurcation lesions with two-stent technique)
devices_driven: guidewire (two guidewires in VasCure) and balloon/stent catheter; master has separate catheter and balloon joysticks; guide catheter advanced manually by the assistant in the pig test (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II-A, III-B)
n_dof_detail: N.R. as a total; per channel guidewire translation + rotation (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II-B) 2015 DRH: thumb 2 DOF + forefinger 3 DOF (feng2015 Sec. II-A).
rotation_detail: other: active and passive rollers translate along their own axes to roll the wire like thumb and forefinger (zhao2021_vascure Sec. II-B); A4/chen2026 review calls it a subjacent lifting mechanism
device_range: N.R. (DRH stated compatible with catheters and balloon/stent catheters of different diameters, wei2020_novel Sec. 2) 2015 tests: guidewire 0.35 mm (0.36 in Table I) and balloon/stent catheter 0.7 mm, displacement limited to 200 mm (feng2015 Sec. III-A, III-D).
force_sensing: proximal: guidewire friction force from motor torque via a T21WN torque sensor (li2024_modelbased Sec. IV-B); no integrated force feedback in VasCure per chen2026_teleoperation (review) 2015 DRH: none; a torque sensor is future work (feng2015 Sec. IV).
haptics_leader: no force feedback reported; master console = guidewire handle (push/pull + rotating knob), catheter joystick, balloon joystick, touchscreen GUI (zhao2021_vascure Fig. 3)
imaging_compat: X-ray fluoroscopy (DSA in pig PCI); EM tracking used for bench accuracy
validation_detail: Remote pig PCI over a 5G commercial network, surgeon about 10 km away, two guidewires to LCX and LAD then balloons along both (zhao2021_vascure Sec. III-B; one pig described); GPC controller PCI on an experimental pig, IAE reduced by at least 20% (zhang2021_improved, abstract); further 5G remote PCI pig trials reported by a review (Han 2023 via chen2026_teleoperation [57], review-level)
key_numbers: VasCure max guidewire error 0.25 mm advance / 0.38 mm retract over 150 mm at 7.2-25.2 mm/s, 10 trials per speed per channel, EM tracker at 40 Hz (zhao2021_vascure Sec. III-A, Tables I-II); DRH mean axial RMSe 0.72 +/- 0.49 mm (wei2020_novel Abstract); review: 5G latency 90 -> 163 ms at 1100 km and 81 -> 161 ms at 18.3 km (chen2026_teleoperation, Han 2023); learning on the robot: CASOG 94.00 +/- 4.32% success (50 deliveries x 3 seeds; human demonstrations 39/42) on a 15 x 15 x 1 cm printed planar phantom (li2023_casog, arXiv HTML Table 2); CORVE 80.33 +/- 5.09% and 84.00 +/- 4.76% vs CASOG 69.67 +/- 2.69% on phantom 1 (li2024_modelbased Table II) 2015 DRH (feng2015 Sec. III): 5 trials per manipulation (guidewire and balloon/stent translation at 10 mm/s, guidewire rotation), speed sweeps 0.5-60 mm/s; RMS errors shown only as bar plots (Fig. 6), no number in the text.
sim_model: group's own guidewire/vessel VR simulators (fast and stable guidewire simulator EMBC 2015; elastic guidewire simulator wang2018_simulator; titles only); no model of the robot found
sim2real_detail: none found: the RL controllers (CASOG, CORVE, discrete SAC, offline-online RL) were trained on data recorded on the physical robot over a planar phantom with an overhead 140 x 140 px camera, not in simulation (li2024_modelbased Sec. III-A, full; li2023_casog Sec. IV, arXiv HTML); li2023_discrete (Robotica 2023, full): DSAC-AE learned guidewire delivery directly on the 2-DOF robot over a 15 x 15 x 1.5 cm 3D-printed planar model, 140 x 140 px overhead images, 10 discrete actions every 0.5 s, success after 50k real samples in < 15 h (Sec. 2.1, 4); the paper argues against training in simulation (Sec. 1)
